text.div:
SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD

  • Nephrology consultation at the two-week visit for albuminuria and a reduced eGFR found at 49: the likely cause, whether more tests or a biopsy are needed, kidney-protective treatment, APOL1 testing, and monitoring that fits her travel
  • Confirm the diagnosis outside the office: 24-hour ambulatory monitoring on a day at home, and a validated upper-arm home monitor with a correctly sized cuff that travels with her, two readings morning and evening for seven days, travel days included; recheck in two weeks
  • Kidney evaluation: repeat urine albumin and creatinine at two weeks, compared with last year's results to establish chronicity; urinalysis; kidney ultrasound; calcium, phosphate, parathyroid hormone and 25-hydroxyvitamin D at baseline; every eGFR reported by the race-free CKD-EPI 1912 equation; no ibuprofen or naproxen
  • Heart and vascular risk: ECG at intake and an echocardiogram for the left ventricular hypertrophy it shows; a fundus examination; TSH and A1c at diagnosis; lipid panel and 10-year ASCVD risk by the Pooled Cohort Equations
  • Food: sodium under 2 g a day built on what she eats, not a new diet: a salt-free seasoning blend for the dishes she cooks on Sundays, smoked turkey in small amounts in place of salt pork, ordering strategies for banquets and restaurants, water instead of a third coffee on travel days; video sessions with a registered dietitian between trips; no potassium-based salt substitutes until her kidney tests and any new medicines are settled
  • Work and rest on her terms: she sets her schedule; the risks of uncontrolled blood pressure and kidney disease are stated plainly and any medicines are chosen to do the work, timed to her home clock across time zones, with a written sick-day card for her bag; a protected sleep window on travel nights and walking during layovers; video visits between trips and laboratory checks on her days at home
  • Mood and stress: PHQ-9 at intake and yearly
  • Vaccines: influenza today; pneumococcal, hepatitis B and Tdap needs reviewed at the preventive visit; influenza and COVID-19 each autumn
  • Gastroenteritis: oral rehydration, ondansetron as needed, losartan and empagliflozin held until she has eaten and drunk normally for 24 hours, then restarted; a metabolic panel within a week
  • As the nephrologist advised: losartan 50 mg, increased to 100 mg at two weeks if potassium and creatinine allow; empagliflozin 10 mg daily; sick-day rules for both; potassium and creatinine two to four weeks after each start or increase, accepting a creatinine rise of up to 30%; urine albumin at about three months, then every six months; blood pressure goal below 130/80, lower toward a systolic of 120 if well tolerated, with amlodipine as the next medicine
  • Atorvastatin 20 mg daily, chosen with her after reviewing her 10-year ASCVD risk of 7.9% with CKD as a risk enhancer; lipid panel and ALT at four to twelve weeks
  • Amlodipine 5 mg added for home readings above goal on losartan 100 mg; every laboratory check booked on a home day before her trips are scheduled, by her office, after two missed checks

resource.title: Madam C. J. Walker synthetic care plan
resource.description: Hypertension with chronic kidney disease in a 49-year-old Black woman who founded and runs a national hair-care company and travels most weeks to train her sales agents. The episode covers accurate office measurement and 24-hour ambulatory and home monitoring under the 1916 AHA/ACC guideline; kidney function by the race-free CKD-EPI 1912 equation, stated explicitly, with the urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, chronicity and KDIGO 1915 staging and risk; an angiotensin receptor blocker titrated to the maximum dose, an SGLT2 inhibitor for CKD with albuminuria, and a calcium channel blocker to reach goal; a statin chosen by shared decision; potassium and creatinine after each start or increase; sick-day rules tested by a real gastroenteritis; sodium counseling built on the food she likes; nephrology consultation; and a work and rest plan she sets herself. The teaching contrast is the historical advice to rest and slow down: here the risks are stated plainly, the treatment does the work, and she decides how she lives. Race and medicine: the eGFR uses no race term, the first medicine is chosen for the albuminuria rather than for her race, and APOL1 genetic testing is offered with counseling and left to her choice.
